summary: My declared family was residual topology / layer connectivity. The headline idea there failed: modded-nanogpt-style U-net skip connections, parameterised as a strict superset of the baseline (zero-init scalars), measured 1.001790 vs 0.997359 baseline -- the existing x0 re-injection already covers them at depth 8, and the extra live activations cost step time. What did work from my family was value-embedding PLACEMENT: moving value embeddings from the shipped alternating set to modded-nanogpt's first-3/last-3 set gave a consistent-sign win on four different bases (-0.0018 at depth-8/dim-512, -0.0005 at depth-10/dim-640, -0.0009 at depth-8/dim-640, -0.0018 at depth-8/dim-768/window-256), i.e. about -0.001 on average for two lines of code and two extra tiny embedding tables. It is redundant with depth increases but additive with width and window changes. My other contribution was combination testing that nobody holding a single lever was positioned to do; my final config (depth 8 / dim 768 / ASPECT_RATIO 96 / short window 256 / first-3-last-3 value embeddings / 197K-token batch at device batch 96) scored 0.976408, the cell best, and is an accidental exact replication of a2's 8c327f6 (0.977161) -- so the honest value is 0.9768 +/- 0.0008 and the 0.00075 spread reproduces the group's noise floor at the frontier rather than at baseline. Next I would attack the LR-schedule shape (WARMDOWN_RATIO / FINAL_LR_FRAC) directly at this frontier config, since a5 only probed it on older, much weaker bases, and I would re-test whether the -0.0018 from value-embedding placement comes from the extra tables or from their position by running first-3/last-3 with only four tables.
